James Brown knew Patrick only as a lifelong Pennsylvania resident; by 1908, Patrick had lived in Schuylkill County for decades with no visible connection to his Irish birth. Brown may never have been told that Patrick was born in Ireland, or may have conflated Patrick's long-established Pennsylvania home with the birthplace itself — a documented pattern when an informant reports birth facts for an earlier immigrant generation without firsthand knowledge of the pre-emigration period.

## Two Dimensions, Separately

These are two independent questions. A document can be *original* yet contain *secondary* information (the death certificate is the classic example, and it's right here in this project).
